headline: Protesters in Calgary and other cities rallied against new data centres on a coordinated North American day of protest.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: fresh event on 3 Oct 2026 and a sign of organized opposition, but a small turnout in one city.
importance_line: Residents near proposed sites now have a cross-border protest movement pressing on water use, secrecy and tax breaks, which Alberta's government must answer as it drafts siting rules, though the Calgary rally drew only a few dozen people.
summary: The Calgary Herald reports that a few dozen people rallied at Calgary City Hall on 3 Oct 2026 as part of a North American Day of Protest Against Data Centres, with events also planned in Edmonton, Lethbridge, Grande Prairie and cities across the continent; organizer Jenna Abbas of Alberta Anti-AI said there is "such a rush to build these data centers" with little environmental assessment. Alberta technology minister Nate Glubish answered that every project must pass independent approvals and environmental reviews and that the province is drafting standards to keep large data centers away from homes.
notes: Full text read. Water use, farmland and a wetland site in Chestermere were the specific local complaints.
